title: The Real Effects of Supply Chain Transparency Regulation – Evidence from Section 1502 of the Dodd-Frank Act

scopes.description: All author-documented branches and supplied companions: Responsible Sourcing (EDGAR preparation, SAS and Stata), Smelters (SAS production plus both Stata exports), and Conflict Minerals (SAS production plus all seven Stata do-files). SAS-created exports are internal producer-to-consumer handoffs in this scope. The two selected in-memory additional-analysis callers also require author-confirmed input and order after SAS production; the generated export set does not resolve that mapping.

A separate, partial prepared-input route for the two Smelters and all seven Conflict Minerals Stata companion do-files. It uses package-local analysis exports without imposing their SAS raw inputs; caller-load setup is required where a do-file starts with data already in memory. The Mining_Region_Sub_Sample export is retained as a bounded-header candidate but has no established selected caller and is not mandatory.

issues.description: The Responsible Sourcing SAS entry actively reads six absent external members; each now has a separate mandatory input contract. Bounded catalog records are product candidates only, and exact source, field, join, period and current access remain unresolved.

The packaged edgar_log_data and handcollected_combined SAS files are read by the author entry, but the bounded metadata helper returned unsupported-character-set/readstat errors for both. Required columns and periods remain unverified.

Author documentation describes 2016 EDGAR log preparation and 2014–2015 SRAF log inputs, while the supplied notebook selects April 2017 SD/SD-A files and refers to an index covering 2016–2017. The intended data period, upstream files and handoff into edgar_log_data need author clarification.

The notebook conditionally merges temp_lookup_df.pkl and temp_error_df.pkl returned through LookupEDGAR. The helper files contain candidate credential/connection statements that the saved reader withheld as whole blocks; the temporary-file producer and request route cannot be verified from the visible text. No candidate values are retained in this report.

The Smelters SAS branch requires smelter_level_data.sas7bdat, which is not in the package. The README also describes a smelter_downloads preparation folder/code that is absent from the inventory; its manual collection, conformance review and RMI fuzzy-match history are not supplied.

All three SAS branch drivers use C-drive LIBNAME, include or export paths. Their package-relative libraries, helper macros and output locations must be mapped consistently in an isolated working copy.
The SAS 9.4 environment startup record fails while loading TKELS, so the author-required SAS runtime remains unverified. The diagnostic is not evidence of absent licensing.

The packaged smelters.dta is under Smelters/Export. One of the two supplied Stata companions points to [redacted-path-b4910de8e4e5] while the other points to [redacted-path-e8e1cfb7677b]. Keep both analyses and map the first to the same packaged export in the working copy.

The Conflict Minerals SAS stage separately reads twelve package-local SAS tables. Eleven bounded metadata probes returned unsupported-character-set/readstat errors; mineral_prices yielded a one-row header only, so full schemas and coverage remain unresolved.

The README places the proc_logistic Stata companion after the SAS stage, and SAS exports Table_1a to the same proc_logistic.dta path. The five-line do-file starts with egen and has no use statement, so the caller must load that same generated file before invoking it. This is ordinary full-pipeline setup; header and row coverage were not independently verified.

Eastern_DRC_do_file.do line 1 opens a quoted use path without a closing double quote. The exact one-character repair remains proposed and unapplied. In full_pipeline the SAS stage produces Eastern_DRC.dta; in analysis_only the same intended file is packaged. Configure the selected route path in a working copy.

The Conflict SAS stage exports TTTG_Mining_Regions.dta, the exact package-local export is present, and its bounded header includes the variables used by the 14-line Stata companion. Because that do-file starts in memory and has no use statement, load this same generated file for full_pipeline or the packaged copy for analysis_only before invoking it. The one-row probe does not establish full period coverage.

Stata 18 is available, but bounded which checks did not find outreg2 and xtpsse (used by the supplied analyses), fect (used in conflict analyses), or tmpdir (called by the supplied spatial helper). These required commands must be identified and made available before later execution.

The supplied Personal ado helpers are present but are not found by default Stata which checks. The README directs users to place the Personal folder on the Stata ado path; this needs a working-copy configuration.

Selected Conflict Minerals Stata helpers read _ids.dta and macro-expanded improve_ids and indata_ids datasets; the reviewed local source context does not establish their producers or caller-side sources. A reg2hdfe error-recovery branch also reads macro origdata without a producer established by the reviewed context. These are unresolved producer/caller mappings, not findings that the referenced files are absent.

Full_Sample_do_file_for_an_additional_analysis.do and Pre_Period_do_file_for_an_additional_analysis.do both start in memory, have no explicit use statement, build panel keys, and use iso_3/iv_cov_country. Their required input fields are recorded in E-ADDITIONAL-CALLER-REVIEW. Five distinct bounded export headers contain those field names, but the README and selected sources do not establish which file or caller order is intended; the one-row headers do not establish sample or period equivalence. Keep the five exports distinct, do not treat Mining_Region_Sub_Sample.dta as mandatory from its filename, and retain this exact mapping/order as unresolved. A later caller must load a fresh author-confirmed data state before each companion because the files modify in-memory variables and observations. This same unresolved mapping applies to both full_pipeline after the Conflict SAS stage and analysis_only with caller-prepared inputs; the existence of raw inputs or generated exports does not identify the intended caller route.

The Folder Conflict_Minerals contains data and codes to replicate the latter 6 tables of this paper. 
-conflicts_in_covered_countries contains the SAS codes we used to generate the datasets we use in our analyses.
These datasets can be found in Exports.  
-The respective Stata do-files for the datasets are available in the folder to reproduce the tables in our paper.  
-ACLED_Full is downloaded from the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data database available at https://acleddata.com/
-Polity data is downloaded from the Polity IV Project database available at http://www.systemicpeace.org/polity/polity4x.htm 
-bcrt_baseline contains the Raw Material Data from Berman, Couttenier, Rohner, and Thoenig (2017) available at https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.20150774
-theglobalecon contains information about country-level economic activities (e.g., GDP-per-capita; labor force; male unemployment rate; and capital investment) from theglobaleconomy.com
-the World Governance Index contains information about the perception of country-level governance (e.g., political stability index)
-plos_mlmv_b contains information about the territories of the Eastern DRC (e.g., 3T and G mines).  
-mineral_prices contains information about the 3TG mineral prices available at World Bank and the U.S. geological survey
-ipis_full contains information about 3TG mines available at https://ipisresearch.be/home/maps-data/

The later retained known-candidate-line comparison found no overlap in those seven ranges. The 20/20 and 42/42 checks remain preserved intermediate history. The current 49/49 source citations match saved redacted_reader.py output, with zero cited-interval overlaps against known candidate lines. The proc_logistic and TTTG files have supported same-data caller-load setup: each is linked to its exact SAS export and the Stata file starts with in-memory commands. One-row metadata does not prove full-period coverage; the current configuration actions address the caller load step without inventing sample data.
